title: Consolidation and Split-Testing Playbook for LLM Deployment
author: Marcus Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook helps field teams and platform engineers run consolidation pilots (migrating multiple smaller LLM endpoints to a unified Redwood deployment) while simultaneously running split-tests to validate model quality, cost, and latency trade-offs. It combines positioning and messaging guidance, a competitive brief (how to counter common objections), an executable pitch deck outline, pricing scenarios and worksheets, a short case study template, and a targeted security FAQ for prospects evaluating consolidation or A/B split-testing strategies.

When to use this playbook:
- Prospect has multiple in-house or multi-vendor endpoints and is evaluating consolidation to reduce unit cost and operational overhead.
- Engineering teams want to validate a migration strategy with canary + split-testing across 1–3 user journeys.
- Platform/infra buyers need clear ROI scenarios tied to latency SLOs and failure-recovery behavior.

Primary objectives:
1. Demonstrate predictable unit economics (tokens/second and $/1M tokens) after consolidation.
2. Maintain or improve latency SLOs (p90 and p99) during rollout.
3. Preserve model quality via split-testing and automated eval gating.
4. Surpass competitor objections on security, vendor lock-in, and migration risk.

Positioning & messaging (battle-tested lines)
- Core message: "Consolidate inference, control economics." Follow with three pillars: predictable performance, measurable unit costs, and flexible deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Quick opener for CTO/Platform: "We help you move from brittle, vendor-sprawled endpoints to a single inference plane that enforces latency SLOs and reduces per-token cost by ~30–60% depending on workload characteristics."
- Quick opener for Security/CISO: "We integrate with KMS/HSM, provide VPC/private deployments, and ship audit-ready logs for model access and data residency controls."

Competitive brief (objections + rebuttals)
- Objection: "We already have optimized on-prem endpoints; why migrate?"
  - Rebuttal: Highlight Redwood's continuous batching and KV caching that reduces cost per token for conversational workloads. Share a mini-benchmark: 40–55% lower token cost vs. single-shot on-prem endpoints for high re-use prefix distributions. Offer a pilot with replayed traffic to quantify.
- Objection: "Vendor lock-in concerns."
  - Rebuttal: Explain model-variant routing, open model catalog, and pin/version controls; show how tokens, prompts, and eval sets can be exported and migrated. Provide TOS excerpts on portability.
- Objection: "Security/compliance risk."
  - Rebuttal: Provide specific artifacts (SOC2 Type II in progress/completed, KMS integrations, VPC mode, on-prem packaging) and reference our security checklist in the demo.

Pitch deck guide (10-slide minimal flow)
1. Title & TL;DR — outcome-oriented one-liner: consolidation ROI and risk mitigation.
2. Customer pain & evidence — map their current endpoint estate and baseline cost/latency.
3. Redwood solution — architecture diagram (hosted + dedicated + private).
4. How consolidation works — traffic routing, canary policies, split-testing flow.
5. Performance evidence — p50/p90/p99 and token unit economics for representative workloads.
6. Security & compliance — KMS, VPC, audit logs, on-prem option.
7. Pilot plan & success criteria — metrics, duration, gating.
8. Pricing scenarios — pay-as-you-go vs. reserved capacity with break-even math.
9. Customer stories & expected outcomes — short case.
10. Next steps & asks — technical contacts, data access, pilot start date.

Pilot design: consolidation + split-testing (step-by-step)
1. Discovery (1 week)
   - Inventory endpoints, sample traffic, SLOs, model families in use.
   - Deliverable: baseline report (RPS, token distribution, p50/p90/p99 latencies, cost per 1M tokens).
2. Pilot config (1 week)
   - Provision Redwood sandbox with matching models.
   - Define split-test: 10% traffic to Redwood consolidated path, 90% to existing systems.
   - Define quality gates: automated eval on 5 key prompt sets and manual review on 50 random conversations.
3. Run & measure (2–4 weeks)
   - Monitor latency (p50/p90/p99), error rates, cost, and quality regressions.
   - Use canary rollback thresholds: if p99 increases >25% or quality degrades >5% on weighted eval, rollback.
4. Scale & optimize (2 weeks)
   - Apply batching and cache suggestions from Redwood Optimize; test quantized variants if cost-sensitive.
5. Finalize commercial ask
   - Present runbook, estimated savings, and recommended capacity commitment.

Success criteria (sample gating)
- Latency: p90 <= baseline p90 * 1.10 and p99 <= baseline p99 * 1.25 during steady-state (excluding cold-start periods).
- Cost: projected $/1M tokens <= baseline $/1M tokens * 0.75 (target 25% savings).
- Quality: automated eval delta <= 2% on primary prompts and manual review shows no critical defects.

Pricing guidance (scenarios & worksheet)
- Recommended approach for sellers: present three scenarios (pilot, scale, dedicated).
- Scenario A — Pilot (no commit): PAYG hosting, estimate usage with buffer. Example: 1M tokens/month = $X (show calculation) — use customer baseline tokens * 1.2 to cover spike risk.
- Scenario B — Scale (6–12 month): Reserved capacity with discount tiers. Example math: 20% discount at 3-month commit, 35% at annual. Show break-even compared to PAYG.
- Scenario C — Dedicated/Private (enterprise): Include platform fee + managed capacity + optional on-prem license. Show example TCO over 12 months including SRE effort saved.

Pricing worksheet (text table)
- Inputs: baseline tokens/month, average token length, request distribution (chat vs. completion), p90 latency requirement.
- Outputs: PAYG monthly cost estimate, reserved monthly cost estimate, projected savings, recommended commit.

Mini case study template (one page for slides)
- Customer: "Online Commerce Platform" (anon)
- Problem: 15 disparate endpoints, unpredictable latency spikes during peak, high token cost.
- Pilot: 30-day consolidation to Redwood hosted + 10% split-test for control.
- Results: 37% reduction in token cost, p90 improved from 420ms -> 260ms, zero customer-facing incidents during migration.
- Quote: "Redwood let us centralize inference without regressing latency — and the cost math was straightforward."

Security FAQ for consolidation & split-testing
Q: How is customer data protected in hosted pilots?
A: Hosted pilots support VPC peering and private endpoints; data in transit is TLS 1.3, data at rest is encrypted using customer-managed KMS keys where required. Audit logs with request-level IDs are available for the pilot.

Q: Can we run split-tests without routing PII to Redwood?
A: Yes. Customers can redact or pseudonymize PII before routing, or run the pilot on a private deployment (VPC or on-prem) to ensure no data leaves the customer boundary.

Q: What compliance evidence can we provide?
A: We can provide SOC2 Type II report summary, penetration test report excerpts, and a deployment checklist showing KMS integrations, VPC config artifacts, and operational runbooks used during the pilot.

Q: What are typical isolation and network options?
A: Hosted with private endpoints, Dedicated in a customer-segregated cluster, VPC peering, and on-prem appliance packaging for air-gapped environments. Each option includes logging/audit and key management controls.

Q: Failure and fallback behavior during split-tests?
A: Redwood supports transparent traffic mirroring, canary traffic with automatic percentage rollback, and automatic fallback to the origin endpoint on error or increased latency per the configured policy. We recommend a max 5xx rate threshold of 1% and p99 latency threshold defined per-customer during pilot config.

Demo artifacts and CLI examples
- Traffic replay (example):
  - rtx-replay --source logs.json --target https://<redwood-sandbox>/ingest --concurrency 20
- Simple curl to exercise a unified API endpoint (chat):
  - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize sales pipeline improvements"}]}'

Rollout playbook (checklist)
1. Preflight: obtain sample traffic, identify 3 critical flows, confirm SLOs.
2. Sandbox: run replay; produce baseline report.
3. Canary: route 5–10% traffic for 48–72 hours. Monitor metrics and quality gates.
4. Ramp: increment in 10–20% steps with 24–48 hour observation windows.
5. Full cutover: switch primary traffic path; retain origin for 14 days in passive mode for quick rollback.
6. Post-mortem: deliver lessons learned and optimize batching/quantization settings.

Appendix: recommended KPIs to track during pilot (minimum)
- Token consumption by route (tokens/request)
- p50/p90/p99 latency per route
- 5xx/error rate per route
- Cost per 1M tokens
- Eval pass rate on guardrail prompt sets
